thread.title: App Store Just Turned 10: Fun Facts, Figures From App Annie

author: Barron's
title: App Store Just Turned 10: Fun Facts, Figures From App Annie
text:
Adam Berry/Getty Images for Apple The late Steve Jobs first broached the idea of a digital store for Apple ( AAPL ) apps in 2008. It was at the Worldwide Developers Conference , and the charismatic Jobs, then CEO, called it the iOS App Store .
A decade later, App Store is a centerpiece of Apple's powerhouse Services division. More than 170 billion apps have been downloaded, totaling more than $130 billion in consumer spending. ( This year's edition of WWDC starts Monday in San Jose, Calif.)
App Annie , which closely tracks App Store and Google Play , issued a fascinating report today that encapsulates the phenomenom. By 2022, it estimates consumer spending on App Store will reach $75.7 billion, up 80% from 2017. Some $53.1 billion is expected to be spent in 2018. Games account for 31% of downloads and 75% of spending.
"Apple completely re-architected media consumption through a touch-input mobile device," Danielle Levitas , senior vice president of research, content, and communications at App Annie, tells Barron's .
Apple, in essence, created the ultimate megastore , an immense marketplace that established it as a major player in e-commerce-without onerous infrastructure costs and overhead. In so doing, it upended the way content providers created, distributed, and monetized programs, especially in gaming. No longer were shoppers forced to visit retail outlets or websites to purchase programs for $50 a pop. Delivery was instant, and the apps were often free.
While App Store is considered one of Jobs', and Apple's, great achievements, it does lag behind Google Play in downloads (70%), although consumers purchase more on App Store (66%).
Some other App Store fun facts, courtesy of App Annie: The top three markets are, in order, the U.S., China, and Japan. The top three downloaded apps worldwide so far this year are PUBG Mobile , Tik Tok , and YouTube .
